A.definition: today's asincrono LRU path, code path unchanged: all kinds waited for at the first expert node; later nodes release and re-acquire the slices as hits

B.definition: A with the research trace on; supplies the one-shot headroom bound (Phase 1b, development prompts) and the mechanism reference (Phase 2)

C.definition: issue exactly as A at the first expert node; wait only for the kind this node consumes; at each later node of the same layer wait only for that node's kind and LRU-touch the layer's slices in A's order; the layer's pins are held until the next layer's first expert node
C.uses_only: the router decision of the current layer (already used by A)

C0_I.definition: C's code path (pins held for the layer, later nodes LRU-touch instead of re-acquire) but every thread waits for ALL its reads at the first expert node, as A. Differs from C only in where the wait happens, so C_I - C0_I isolates overlap from cheaper bookkeeping. Never in the timing campaign, never in the classification except through G4.

C_I.definition: C with the research trace on

common_environment.binary: the single R5 build frozen at the implementation freeze; all arms of all campaigns use the same binary
common_environment.end_of_run_counters: every launch of every arm writes one end-of-run record of store counters (misses, bytes_read, evictions, budget violations, pending reads at graph end)

excluded: retention policies and the blocco read mode
changes to budgets, thread counts, read mode or kernels
invariants_C_vs_A: same set of slices requested per layer, the frozen issue order, same bytes read
same LRU access sequence (later-node hits replaced by psx_cache_touch in the same order); misses, miss bytes and evictions within the purity tolerance
same pinned footprint (no extra residency); budget violations 0; no pending read at the end of any graph
no prediction, no lookahead across layers, no new thread, no tunable parameter
identical generated tokens (greedy decoding on identical weights and kernels)
issue_order: A's current order, frozen: at the first expert node of a layer the slices are indexed k = 0 .. n_serve*n_kinds-1 with kind = k / n_serve over the kind list [this node's kind, then the remaining kinds in enum order gate, up, down] and expert = the k % n_serve-th selected expert in ascending id; threads claim k dynamically from one shared atomic counter. C and C0 must issue exactly this sequence (verified by a model-free test that records the claimed (k, kind, expert) sequence).

oracle_E.definition: the trace-derived hideable bound H of ENDPOINTS.json, computed once from B launches on development prompts; it characterises headroom only and is never a policy, an arm or a result in favour of R5; it is loose (W spans to the last expert node although node-2 reads can only hide behind node-1 compute)

stronger_causal_scheduler_D.reason: The runtime offers no further causally known information before a layer's router runs (F2). A 'stronger' causal scheduler of the same information would differ only in wait placement, which C already moves to the latest correct point. Any scheduler that issues layer-L reads earlier needs predicted expert ids, which is Research 2-4 territory and is excluded. A second variant would only add multiplicity.

trace_symmetry: B, C0_I and C_I write the identical set of trace record types and fields (fields that do not apply are written empty), so trace overhead is the same in every traced arm; the per-arm trace overhead is reported on development prompts
